slides.0.subtitle: Level 1 · Module 3 · Lesson 4
slides.1.title: Coonawarra: The Terra Rossa Strip
slides.1.points.0: Location: Limestone Coast Zone, 380 km southeast of Adelaide
slides.1.points.1: Famous for: terra rossa (red iron-rich topsoil over limestone bedrock) — a narrow strip ~15 km × 2 km
slides.1.points.2: Climate: cool continental; Cabernet reaches perfect phenolic ripeness slowly
slides.1.points.3: Key varieties: Cabernet Sauvignon (60%), Shiraz, Merlot
slides.1.points.4: Style: Cabernet with mint, eucalyptus, blackcurrant and firm structure — unique to this terroir
slides.2.title: Terra Rossa: Why Soil Matters Here
slides.2.points.0: Terra rossa = red soil derived from iron oxide deposited on ancient limestone seabed
slides.2.points.1: Free-draining: vines must work hard to find water → stress → concentration
slides.2.points.2: Limestone sub-soil: regulates water table; roots can penetrate deep for minerals
slides.2.points.3: The narrow terra rossa strip is the most prized land — outside it, black rendzina soil produces different results
slides.2.points.4: Australia's most discussed and contested terroir — the GI boundary was legally disputed for 20+ years
slides.3.title: Top Coonawarra Producers
slides.3.points.0: 🏆 Wynns Coonawarra Estate: Australia's largest and most historic Coonawarra estate; Black Label Cabernet is iconic
slides.3.points.1: 🦁 Penley Estate: premium Cabernet and Merlot; modern approach
slides.3.points.2: 🌿 Balnaves of Coonawarra: family estate; The Tally Reserve Cabernet is benchmark
slides.3.points.3: 🍷 Parker Coonawarra Estate: Terra Rossa First Growth Cabernet competes with world's best
slides.3.points.4: 🌳 Katnook Estate: highly regarded Odyssey Cabernet
slides.4.question: What is 'terra rossa' and why is it important to Coonawarra?
slides.4.options.0: An Italian red wine variety grown in Coonawarra
slides.4.options.1: A narrow strip of red iron-rich topsoil over limestone that creates perfectly drained, stress-inducing conditions for Cabernet
slides.4.options.2: A red-painted building where Coonawarra wines are stored
slides.4.options.3: A local marketing term with no geologic basis
slides.4.explanation: Terra rossa is iron-rich red topsoil deposited on ancient limestone bedrock. This combination provides excellent drainage (preventing waterlogging), forces vine roots deep into limestone for minerals, and stresses vines just enough to produce small, concentrated Cabernet Sauvignon berries. The thin terra rossa strip in Coonawarra (~15 × 2 km) is Australia's most famous and most legally contested terroir.
slides.5.title: Lesson Summary
slides.5.points.0: Coonawarra: narrow terra rossa strip over limestone → benchmark SA Cabernet
slides.5.points.1: Distinctive mint/eucalyptus + blackcurrant style from cool continental climate
slides.5.points.2: Top producers: Wynns (benchmark), Parker (world-class), Balnaves, Penley
